column2: On the authority of Ibn Masʿūd (may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The blood of a Muslim person is not lawful except in one of three cases: the married adulterer, a life for a life, and the one who leaves his religion and separates from the community.” Reported by al-Bukhārī and Muslim.

His words, “the married adulterer”: al-thayyib is one who is muḥṣan [has been in a valid marriage], and his ruling is stoning, as established in the Sunnah from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and as indicated by the verse of stoning, whose recitation was abrogated while its ruling remained.

His words, “a life for a life”, mean killing in retaliation, as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: “O you who believe, retaliation is prescribed for you in the case of those killed…” [al-Baqarah 2:178], to the end of the verse; and He said: “And there is life for you in retaliation” [al-Baqarah 2:179].
His words, “the one who leaves his religion and separates from the community”: what is meant is the apostate from Islam,
because he ﷺ said: “Whoever changes his religion, kill him.” Reported by al-Bukhārī (3017).

The ḥāfiẓ Ibn Rajab mentioned the killing of a number of others besides those mentioned in the hadith: [those who commit] sodomy, one who has intercourse with a woman within the prohibited degrees, the sorcerer, one who has intercourse with an animal, one who abandons the prayer,

the drinker of wine on the fourth occasion, the thief on the fifth occasion, the second of two caliphs to whom allegiance has been given, one who brandishes weapons [against people], and the Muslim spy who spies on the Muslims for the disbelievers.
The inviolability of a Muslim's blood, unless he commits one of these three.
The ruling for the married adulterer is death by stoning.
Killing one who has killed deliberately, in retaliation, when the conditions of retaliation are met.
Killing one who apostatises from the religion of Islam, whether male or female.
